thread:
Maya: Quick heads-up — AcmeHealth wants an EU-only POC with BYO-KMS. They explicitly called out 'no control plane outside EU' in their security questionnaire. Can SE/ops/legal confirm what we can commit to for a short POC, and a rough cost delta vs hosted? cc @Ben @Chloe @Dave :pray:

Ben: On it. Two quick clarifying q's: 1) Is the requirement only for data plane (at-rest + egress) or for control-plane/signalling too? 2) Do they need VPC peering or is IP allowlist sufficient?

Erin (acct): From the security questionnaire: "Control plane must be within EU and not route metadata to non-EU subprocessors." They prefer VPC peering but said allowlist could be OK for POC if we provide additional attestation.

Chloe: Legal note — if control plane must be in-EU we can't offer that on Hosted today (control plane runs in us-central). Private deployment or Dedicated with EU control-plane locality is required for contractual commit. For initial POC we can offer a limited attestation + technical mitigations, but not a legal guarantee unless on Dedicated/Private.

Dave: Ops check — current sub-processor footprint touching eu-west-1 data: AWS (eu-west-1), Cloudflare edge POPs (EU), and our managed HashiCorp Vault in eu-west-1 for secret storage. Control-plane signaling currently uses GCP us-central and some control messages land in us. BYO-KMS integration can keep key material in eu-west-1; we support external keystores via mutual TLS/HSM connector.

Ben: Routing/fallback options we can offer for the POC: 1) Tenant pin to eu-west-1 with strict fail-close (reject requests if capacity exhausted). 2) Tenant pin to eu-west-1 with EU-only failover to eu-west-2 (if capacity) 3) Soft-fail to hosted fallback (US) — not acceptable for this customer. Example config we can push for the POC:

```yaml
tenant_region: eu-west-1
routing_policy:
  fallback: eu-west-2
  allow_cross_region: false
  failure_mode: reject
```

Maya: Nice. Can you also capture which subprocessors would see metadata vs payload? They flagged any subprocessors that could see customer metadata as a blocker.

Dave: Payload (model inputs/outputs) will stay in EU when tenant pinned and BYO-KMS enabled. Metadata (request telemetry, traces) currently flows to control plane in us-central for hosted — so that's the blocker. Subprocessors seeing metadata: GCP logging (us-central) and Sentry (if enabled) — both can be disabled for this tenant for the POC.

Chloe: For the questionnaire we should provide: 1) subprocessor list filtered for eu-west-1, 2) data flow diagram showing control vs data plane, 3) BYO-KMS integration steps and attestation language. I'll draft attestation saying telemetry will be disabled and control-plane locality is a proposed mitigation (but not a legal replacement for Dedicated/Private).

Ben: Action items for SE: produce a 1-page ops runbook + config snippet and a cost delta estimate. Rough numbers now?

Dave: Very rough cost delta (POC-scale): Hosted with strict EU-only routing + BYO-KMS (manual attestation, no CP locality) — ~+$2k/mo in ops overhead and engineering time. Dedicated (small reserved pool to guarantee CP+DP locality, SLA) — starting around ~$10k/mo for minimal reserved capacity and infra. These are back-of-envelope; I'll flesh out after we size the traffic (tokens/sec).

Erin: They'll start with a low throughput POC (100 reqs/hr, avg 200 tokens). Use that for sizing please. They want pricing for a 30-day pilot and also what we'd need to commit contractually if they go into prod.

Ben: Got it. I'll put together the pilot-runbook + a short comparison table (Hosted w/attestation vs Dedicated w/CP locality) and post by EOD.

Dave: Ops ETA: create tenant pin, disable non-EU telemetry, wire BYO-KMS test connector, and capture network trace. ETA 2 business days. I'll open a ticket now.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: INF-5231 — "POC AcmeHealth EU-BYO-KMS" assigned to Dave.

Maya: Thanks — Chloe, can you confirm attestation language + whether Cloudflare EU POPs are acceptable for them by EOD? Ben/Dave, ping me when runbook + ticket details + cost estimate are ready. :thumbsup: 

Chloe: Will do. If customer insists on *no* control-plane outside EU we need to scope Dedicated/Private and a timeline for provisioning (usually 2–4 weeks minimum). I'll call that out in the attestation.

Ben: Uploading draft runbook to the thread in 30m.

Erin: FYI I've told the customer we can land a POC in ~2 business days for technical validation (without CP locality). If they escalate legal will ask for Dedicated.

Maya: Perfect — keep this thread for updates.
